newsitem.title: USA: PHLX gets OK to cut select minumum opening trades.
newsitem.headline: PHLX gets OK to cut select minumum opening trades.

text.p: The Philadelphia Stock Exchange (PHLX) said it received U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) approval to cut the minimum opening trade size for customized currency options transactions.
The minimum opening transaction will now be 50 contracts, down from 100, which will be the equivalent of $2.25 million in underlying value compared with $4.5 million previously, the exchange said.
It said the change will apply to all customizable currency options traded on its United Currency Options Market (UCOM).

In addition, all customized currency options contracts set to expire on or after April 1, 1997 will stop trading at 0800 EST (1300 GMT) and will expire at 1015 EST (1515 GMT), with assignments performed on a pro-rata basis, the PHLX said.
Any customized mid-month or end-month contracts scheduled to expire before April 1 will stop trading at 1430 EST (1930 GMT) and expire at 2359 EST (0459 GMT).
The exchange said the change in exercise and assignment times only affects its customized currency options.
